review: Prereg of I69 (= I36a: Bundle I's extraction and acquisition, no laws) at 2fefb519283d4857ae22d432ffb4faca5dde3273, on branch claude/brave-wright-2c5d0o-i36, base e215fbf5 (the lead after I32's build). It covers the BUILD_PLAN row I69 (fa762877); the key I69 in spec/M3/predictions.json; the contract, which is the docstring of tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py (E1-E7, M1-M6, L1-L8, C1-C6, A1-A7, shared files, commit rules and own commits); the instrument tests_m3/_i69.py over tests_m3/_i63.py; the sidecar spec/M3/lib/bundle.json; the basis spec/M3/lib/bundle_basis.json; and the prompt prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md. Read alongside: AGENTS.md; docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md (Q7, Q12, Q18, Q19); the drafter's design notes; and the precedent reviews of I66 and I28, checked for the same defect classes. Sources were read in /root/work/morph through git objects only, with lazy fetching disabled. Nothing from scroll-tech or spec/heldout was read. No network, no holon run or gate on M3, and holon's frontend and model3 were not run on any new member.
verdict_note: No blocking finding. The mechanics are clean: both prereg audits exit 0, FROZEN OK, no frozen file is touched, the 7 tests that should be green at the prereg are green, and the 16 that need the build are red for the right reason. Every number I could recompute matches the key: action names, families, inherited counts, constants, the 28 link rows, the debt lists, the closures, the record counts, the basis, the tree listings and the sidecar's facts. No earlier test needs an amendment for I69's new paths, and none of the claims pins a storage encoding. I do not sign off, because five major findings should be folded in before the freeze. M1 and M2: the own-commit rule ends at the first commit that adds the report and walks the lead's first-parent line, so build commits after a draft report escape R2, and another key's direct lead commit fails it. Both are reproduced with the test's own functions. M3: the instrument's timeline takes the upgrades, implementations and proxy addresses from holon's snapshot unchecked, so P1 and P2 are not independently decided. M4: nothing pins the 427-trace corpus on which P5-P7 are decided. M5: the member models' refinement compares no return data, so P5 says nothing about 15 view actions, or about the fee and reward values that I36b's laws will read. The nine minor findings concern construction facts counted inside P4, P6, P1 and P7 (now computed, so they must be disclosed), the scope of the target-name check, R2 against the amendment route, link reach decided on the machine's own record, A7's uncommitted second read, the unspecified environment for code reads, ownership of future re-makes, the BUILD_PLAN row, and two cheap regressions that R1 omits.

findings.where: tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:224-226 (the docstring's 'Own commits'), :325-340 (own_commits: `end = added[0]` at :328-329), :712-765 (I69-R2); spec/M3/predictions.json:2357 (I69-R2); prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:173-180 (the commit sequence)
findings.what: own_commits() ends at the OLDEST commit that adds docs/iterations/I69.md and walks `git log --first-parent <prereg>..<end>`. The house pattern commits a draft report before the review and its fixes: I26's draft was followed by 14 build commits, and I32's draft 27d08ab8 by its review-fix commit e271fc06 and two report commits (docs/iterations/I28_prereg_review.json, M2). Reproduced on a toy repository with this file's own own_commits() and test_r2_own_commits_touch_nothing_forbidden, with T.ROOT redirected (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-HOLON/36cc748b-c392-5d49-873b-8207b8fa8fb5/scratchpad/i69rev/toy_owncommits.py). Branch i69: prereg, 'build: extraction' (adds gen/M3/bundle/bundle.json), 'report (draft)', 'review fix' (edits laws/M3/L_x.json and spec/M3/lib/bundle.json), 'report (final)'; merged into the lead with --no-ff. Result: own_commits() = ['build: extraction', 'report (draft)'], and I69-R2 PASSES although an own commit edits laws/ and spec/. The converse also holds: if gen/M3/bundle/bundle.json is first added after a draft report, R2 fails with 'no own commit adds gen/M3/bundle/bundle.json'.
findings.why: R2 is the only check of I69's commit rules, including the rule that the M1, M2 and T32 re-make changes generator_sha256 and seconds alone. As written it is silently partial, or falsely red, depending on when the report is first committed.
findings.fix: End at the build branch's tip, found by ancestry, as I66's re-scope of I32-R2 does (tests_m3/test_disch_profile.py at c348daaa, i32_merge and own_commits). R is the oldest commit adding docs/iterations/I69.md (git log --full-history). M is the oldest merge of `git rev-list --ancestry-path --merges R..HEAD` whose second parent reaches R and whose first parent does not. Own commits are the non-merge commits of `git log --first-parent M^2 ^M^1 ^<prereg>`, ending at M^2; before M exists, those of `--first-parent <prereg>..HEAD`. Write this into the docstring before the freeze.

findings.where: tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:224-226 and :325-340 (the first-parent walk); prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:26 ('I69's build starts after that merge') and :182; the lead's first-parent history (476b02bc, 25303315, bb128f43 and e0cbb429 are non-merge commits made directly on the lead)
findings.what: From a build branch that starts on the lead, `git log --first-parent <prereg>..<end>` walks back along the lead's first-parent line until it meets an ancestor of the prereg commit. Two cases. If the prereg lands by a merge commit, that line holds every lead commit after e215fbf5 (the prereg's base) that is not in the prereg's history. If it lands directly, as I32's prereg 476b02bc did, the line holds every lead commit after it. Every non-merge commit there counts as I69's. The lead does commit directly: 476b02bc changed spec/M3/predictions.json, spec/M3/lib and tests_m3; e0cbb429 changed results/M3; 25303315 changed whitepaper.md; bb128f43 changed the M1 and M2 records. Reproduced on a toy repository (toy B in the same script). The lead holds base, 'I70 prereg (pushed directly onto the lead)' (adds spec/M3/lib/other_key.json) and 'Merge PR: I69 prereg'. The build branch starts from that lead, commits 'build: extraction' and 'report', and is merged with --no-ff. Result: own_commits() = ['I70 prereg (pushed directly onto the lead)', 'build: extraction', 'report'], and I69-R2 FAILS ('a forbidden path') although I69's own commits are clean. The prompt itself says the build starts after I66's PR #46 merges, that is, on a lead that has moved past e215fbf5.
findings.why: R2 would report a miss for another key's prereg, or for a lead-side re-make or metrics commit. This is the cross-key hazard of the I28 verification's N1, which I66's re-scope of I32-R2 fixed for I32.
findings.fix: M1's ancestry selection handles the merged case, because ^M^1 excludes the whole lead. For the case before the merge, add two commit rules to the docstring. First, the build branch starts at the prereg commit (not at a lead commit) and takes later lead changes only by merge commits. Second, the prereg reaches the lead only through a merge commit: no direct push and no fast-forward. Then `--first-parent <prereg>..HEAD` on the build branch holds I69's commits alone.

findings.where: tests_m3/_i69.py:495-528 (timeline), :451-469 (decode); tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:620-662 (P1 and P2); docstring A3 (:184-197), A6 (:200-201) and A7 (:202-205); spec/M3/lib/bundle.json:24-27 (the EIP-1967 slots, which no rule reads); spec/M3/predictions.json:2315-2324
findings.what: timeline() does not recompute the timeline. It iterates px['upgrades'] as holon's fetch listed them (:508). For each entry it reads the receipt file named by u['tx'] and checks only that the file hashes to u['receipt_sha256'], a value holon also wrote. It then matches the code file named by u['implementation'] (:514, :522). Things it never checks: (1) that u['implementation'] is the Upgraded topic decoded from that receipt (dec['upgraded'] is recorded but not compared; P1's test checks u1's implementation only against the placeholder, again read from the snapshot); (2) that the entry's block, tx and log_index match the receipt's own transactionHash, blockNumber, logs and status; (3) that the upgrade list comes from the snapshot's raw 'logs' (P1's 'exactly two Upgraded logs' is just the length of holon's list); (4) that the snapshot's proxy addresses are the sidecar's (P2's test never reads tl['proxies']['queue' or 'submitter']['address']); (5) that snap['whitelist']['address'] is the low 20 bytes of its 'word', read at the queue document's whitelistChecker slot (:525-527). The sidecar lists the EIP-1967 implementation slot (bundle.json:24-27), but no rule reads it to anchor each proxy's last implementation. A7's second-provider read covers receipts and code, not the eth_getLogs scan.
findings.why: P1 and P2 are said to be 'decided on tests_m3/_i69.py::timeline's recomputation from the committed snapshot'. Yet a snapshot that names a wrong implementation, misses an upgrade or records the wrong proxy would decide them. Independence fails exactly at the facts these two predictions are about.
findings.fix: Strengthen timeline() and rules A4-A6 in five ways. First, rebuild each proxy's upgrade list from its 'logs' entries whose topic is Upgraded. Second, require each entry to match a receipt whose transactionHash, blockNumber, status and log at log_index agree, and whose decoded Upgraded topic is the implementation whose code is matched. Third, require the proxies' addresses to be the sidecar's (the messenger's is the queue's MESSENGER word), and every log to lie inside the window. Fourth, require the whitelist address to be the word's low 20 bytes at the queue document's whitelistChecker slot. Fifth, add to A3 an eth_getStorageAt of each proxy's EIP-1967 implementation slot at the fetch block, commit it, and check that it equals the last implementation or that a later Upgraded log exists. Finally, have A7 repeat the log scan's counts on the second host and commit that read (see m5).

findings.where: docstring C3 (:142-152) and C6 (:166-171); tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:571-616 (P6, P7, test_corpus_reproduces); spec/M3/lib/bundle.json 'corpus'; holon/mreplay.py:214-233 (random_corpus); results/M2/refinement/extracted.json 'corpus'
findings.what: Nothing pins the 427-trace corpus on which P5-P7 are decided. The only corpus checks are three. refinement.json's own corpus.path and sha256 point at gen/M3/bundle/corpus.json. Its 'sources' counts equal {300, 7, 120}, but holon writes those counts; they are not counted from corpus.json. And `holon bundle corpus --check` is holon reproducing holon. No test compares the seed part with the sidecar's seven planted traces. No test compares the m1 part with I20's corpus. That part is regenerated by holon.mreplay.random_corpus on the compiled M1 model, and both are in the closures I69 edits. No test compares the random part with C3. Nor can C3's text reproduce it: it names no RNG and no draw order, and it pools arguments from the 'event words or return words' of earlier steps, so generating it means executing steps (on holon's machine, since --check runs no forge). The evidence for P5-P7 (refinement.json and refinement_models.json) is aggregate only, with no per-step record that the instrument could recount.
findings.why: P6 ('no disagreement on all 427 traces') and P7 ('every link and action reached') are only as strong as the corpus. The prompt says 'A row no trace reaches is a miss, never a corpus edit after the prereg', but no frozen check enforces it.
findings.fix: Make the instrument check the corpus, in four steps. Require corpus.json's seed traces to equal the sidecar's, after the stated @-name translation. Pin the m1 part's sha256 at the prereg, computed now from I20's inputs as the basis is, or check it against I20's committed corpus. Define the random generator exactly (for example random.Random(20261023), a fixed draw order, and argument pools drawn from the sidecar and earlier arguments only), and regenerate it in the instrument. Count the sources from corpus.json. Also commit per-step evidence (the harness's raw observations per step, or their digests and frames), so that the instrument can recount frames_ok, by_member_action and links_ok.

findings.where: docstring M4 (:88-94); spec/M3/predictions.json:2335 (P5: 'status, revert key, the member's writes and logs'); tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:544-561; results/M3/sorts/refinement.json (I30, M4's precedent): observables ['events', 'revert', 'status', 'storage']; contrast C5 (:159-165), which compares return data
findings.what: M4 compares 'status, revert key, the member's storage writes and its logs (I20's observables)', and no return data. Fifteen of the 49 non-initializer actions are views or pure functions whose only result is the return value: the messenger's messageNonce, owner, paused and verifyMerkleProof; the queue's nextCrossDomainMessageIndex, getCrossDomainMessage, estimateCrossDomainMessageFee, calculateIntrinsicGasFee, computeTransactionHash, getFirstUnfinalizedMessageEnqueueTime, getMessageEnqueueTimestamp and owner; the Whitelist's isSenderAllowed; and the Submitter's isActive and owner. On every top-level step of these, P5 compares status and revert key alone. Submitter.slash's return value, the reward the Rollup credits, is never compared on the model either. M1 makes the evaluator produce ABI-encoded return data, and M2 says model3 compiles the same terms, but no check reads a model's return values.
findings.why: The member models exist for I36b's laws. O29 is about the fee estimateCrossDomainMessageFee returns, and D8's accounting reads slash's reward. A model that returns wrong values still passes P5. This is the one-sided-refinement class (the I28 review's M4).
findings.fix: In M4, compare return data whenever both sides end ok, as C5 does. Also state in M4 that storage is compared at every slot that a write of the step touches on either side.

findings.where: spec/M3/predictions.json:2330 (P4), :2340 (P6), :2315 (P1), :2345 (P7), thresholds.structure (:2643) and links (:2852); tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:486-506 and :524-541 (R5's E2 check); holon/frontends/solidity/transitions.py:3592-3594 (storage, inherited_storage and constants taken from the compiled layout); prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:111 ('It was not run on a new member')
findings.what: Parts of P4, P6, P1 and P7 are fixed at the prereg by solc and committed data, and this review computed them with the instrument alone (tests_m3/_i69.py ast_actions and build at each member's commit; script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-HOLON/36cc748b-c392-5d49-873b-8207b8fa8fb5/scratchpad/i69rev/e2_layouts.py). Rule E2 gives exactly the predicted action lists for all five documents (27, 16, 17, 15 and 4). solc's layout and AST give exactly the predicted own families, inherited counts (13, 5, 1 and 7) and constants. R5's construction check requires every document's action names to equal the instrument's E2, and the frontend copies families, inherited entries and constants from the compiled layout. Rule L2, run on the committed Rollup document with callee stubs built from those names and families, reproduces the 12 Rollup rows of thresholds.links exactly. P7's '49 actions' follows from E2. P1's OTHER_STAKING word is fixed by the constructor (`Staking(_messenger, payable(Predeploys.L2_STAKING))`, L1Staking.sol:93 at v0.6.1). Separately, P4's 'none elsewhere' for constants is not checked for L1Staking: the test at :501 skips storage, inherited entries and constants whenever a structure entry has no 'storage' key.
findings.why: Once R5 holds, these parts cannot miss. They dilute P4, whose open parts are the loop records and cost spans, and they dilute P6 and P7. Now that this review has computed them, they are known facts and must be disclosed as such.
findings.fix: Move these parts to R5 as construction checks, or compute and pin them in the instrument. Disclose this review's computation. Keep in P4 the loop records and cost spans, and in P6 the 16 non-Rollup rows and the refinement.

findings.where: docstring E7 (:65-66); tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:767-790 (R4); tests_m2/test_target_agnostic_exhaustive.py:1-25 (derives its names from spec/M1/facts only)

findings.where: tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:725 (`never = frozen + ('spec/', 'holon/rules/')`); prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:273 ('A wrong instrument is a Question plus an amendment line in spec/M3/amendments.jsonl')
findings.what: R2 bans spec/ in every own commit, so the contract's own route for correcting an instrument fails it. An I69 amendment line in spec/M3/amendments.jsonl, committed on the build branch, is an own commit that changes spec/. The same holds for a separate commit that folds this review into the key: prereg_commit() is the first commit holding I69 (2fefb519), so any later commit that edits the key is an own commit.
findings.why: The sanctioned way to correct an instrument fails I69's own regression, and so would a fold made as a new commit.
findings.fix: Exempt from R2 the lines appended to spec/M3/amendments.jsonl whose iteration is I69 (the file is append-only). Fold this review by amending the prereg commit, as done so far, not by a later commit that touches spec/ or the key.

findings.what: links_ok counts 'L2's rows with the number of their ok executions'. Only the machine's L8 record knows a row's source site, and C5 does not compare the machine's frames with the harness's. frames_ok is 'as the harness recorded them', but what is committed is holon's aggregate of it. For each of the 28 rows the triple (member, action, called function) is unique, so the harness's frames (caller, callee, selector, outcome) could decide link reach independently.
findings.why: Suppose the machine answered a member call from the harness's record (the L7 path) instead of running the callee (L4). It would still agree in every observable C5 compares, and it could still report the link as executed.
findings.fix: Decide links_ok from the harness's frames: caller member, callee, selector and ok. Compare the machine's frames with the harness's in C5, and commit the per-step frames so that the instrument can recount both.

findings.what: Under A7, the review agent re-reads receipts and code from a second host. A differing sha256 makes the predictions that read it UNKNOWN by an override in the report, while their tests stay green. Nothing commits the second read (its host, block and per-file sha256), and the read does not cover the log scan (see M3).
findings.why: An UNKNOWN that rests on a reviewer's note is not mechanical, and the outcome table can then disagree with the tests.
findings.fix: Commit the second read as results/M3/bundle/second_read.json: the host, the methods, each receipt's and each code file's sha256, and the per-proxy log counts. Add a test that compares it with the snapshot, so that the UNKNOWN rule is a check.

findings.where: docstring L1 (:100), L3 (:106-109), L5 (:118-121), L7 (:123-126), C5 (:159-165) and M4; L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle.sol:312 and Submitter.sol:51 at 3e44e795; holon/frontends/solidity/transitions.py:49 and :2176-2177 (['code', a]); holon/extracted_eval.py:673 (answered from a 'code' table); prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:134-140 (the risk list)
findings.what: The queue's appendEnforcedTransaction reads `_sender.code.length` ('only EOA'); seed S5 calls it with _sender = @rollup, a member with code. Submitter.initialize reads `rollupContract_.code.length`. The frontend renders these reads as ['code', a], which the evaluator answers from an environment table. L1-L8, C5 and M4 say where the answers to calls come from, but not where code, or a non-member's balance, comes from. L3 and L5 also give no order for one case: a nested call to a member already on the frame stack, with a selector that is no action, which the compiler's dispatcher reverts with empty data. Random steps reach that case, for example queue.updateWhitelistChecker(@messenger) followed by a sendMessage.
findings.why: Either gap could make a corpus step 'unsupported' or disagree: a P5 or P6 miss caused by the contract, not a fact about the code. The prompt's risk list does not mention the code read.
findings.fix: State in C2 and C5 that every ['code', a] and every balance a step reads is answered from the deployment record (the members and the harness have code; the actors have none), or else recorded by the harness. State that L3's dispatcher revert applies before L5. Add .code.length to the risk list.

findings.where: prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:168 and :171 ('I68 ... The member models follow it'); docstring M3 (:81-87); R5's --check tests (tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:506-510, :563-566, :612-616)
findings.what: gen/M3/bundle/documents, models and corpus, and the refinement records, are outputs of holon.frontends.solidity, model3, extracted_eval and mreplay. I68 (structural storage keys in model3), I28's build (the shared E3 mechanism, and model3 for V3..V10), I36b and I37 (extractor extensions) all change that code. findings.where: docs/BUILD_PLAN.md:344 (row I69, dependencies 'I19, I20, I63'), :314 (row I36), :315 and :322 (I37 and I44 depend on I36), :1243-1261 (I36's deliverables); prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:26

findings.where: docstring E6 (:63-64), M1 (:69-76), M5 (:95) and R1 (tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:685-708); holon/gate.py:376-395 (gate-M2's G1 regenerates gen/M2/extracted/{model.bend, layout.json, window_check.json} with machine.write_model, and results/M2/refinement/extracted.json with holon fragments); gen/M3/{undo,fact,disch}/models/
findings.what: The contract lists holon/machine.py and holon/extracted_eval.py among the files I69 edits. Their M2 outputs, I20's extracted model and refinement record, are checked only by CI's full gate-M2 (R3). R1 is green at the prereg and runs locally in about 3 s, but it covers only the M3 typed and untyped models, not gen/M2/extracted/model.bend. findings.where: prompts/I69_bundle_extraction.md:125-130 (the readings for Q67); L1Staking.sol at v0.6.1 (4a1607db)
findings.what: The five code readings match the v0.6.1 source as I read it. (1) register requires stakingValue at :165, while claimWithdrawal pays the current value (:325) and slash counts it (:224, :227). (2) slash calls _msgRemoveStakers with no value (:243, :486-491); the messenger requires msg.value >= fee + value (L1CrossDomainMessenger.sol:291 at the head), and the queue waives the fee only for whitelisted senders or when l2BaseFee is 0 (:113-119). (3) getStakersFromBitmap's uint8 counter (:426, where `i <= 255` is always true) overflows with Panic 0x11 when no bit 1..255 is set, so slash(0) and slash(1) revert. Since Solidity 0.7, `1 << i` with a literal left operand is computed in uint256, so bits 8..255 are found. (4) verifySignature returns true (:333-341). (5) The Rollup's receive has empty effects and no guard in the adopted document.
findings.why: Checked so that Q67 can be answered on verified readings.

findings.what: Both rely on git's default history simplification. They work on the topologies I tried, but I66 uses --full-history for the same lookup.

findings.where: tests_m3/test_bundle_extraction.py:234-238 (the docstring cites 'PR #46, head c348daaa'); spec/M3/predictions.json thresholds.coordination

open_questions.Q65: Matching the tag source to the deployed bytecode is an acceptable substitute for the explorer's verified source. Q12's condition is that the source compiles to the deployed bytecode with metadata stripped, and an explorer's verification is itself such a match. Here the masked immutables are also checked by value (P1, P2). Three conditions. First, the second provider is an acceptable anchor only if its read is committed and checked by a test (m5). Second, the instrument must actually recompute the timeline from raw logs and receipts (M3). Third, P1's 'exactly two Upgraded logs' needs an anchor for the completeness of the log scan, such as the proxies' EIP-1967 implementation slot at the fetch block, or an archive read at the window's end if the human provides an endpoint. The session environment also exposes an explorer connector. If the human allows it, the build review could compare the verified source with v0.6.1's unit and report any difference under Surprises.
